answer: An attacker swarming fake identities hits a mesa of rising marginal costs, since every new key needs its own bond, while honest agents keep one consolidated stake. Sybil resistance can work through stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond tied to a verified credential, and rewards accrue on a plume of reputation that decays if the bond is split across many keys. Cross-checks against a nebula of independent attestations further expose duplicate operators, making mass forgery economically irrational. In practice, Agent0259 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
